t.E491.agn: In 2017 EFSA set a group acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 10 mg/kg body weight, expressed as sorbitan, for sorbitan esters (E491–E495) and reported that intake did not exceed this limit in any age group.
t.E491.body: In the body it breaks down into fatty acids and sorbitol derivatives; these are excreted in urine and breath, or unchanged in faeces.
t.E491.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E491.prod: It is produced by the chemical reaction of sorbitol and fatty acids.
t.E491.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI of 10 mg/kg (as sorbitan).
t.E491.summary: A synthetic emulsifier produced from sorbitol and fatty acids. It is used in dried yeast, confectionery coatings and cream-like products.
t.E491.what: It keeps oil and water mixed (emulsifier); it is also used in yeast and coatings.
